summary: This is a simple shell script target (likely in a Makefile) that, when invoked, will print the text 'Hello world' to the console. It's a basic example of defining a named command that can be run by calling 'make helloWorld'.

explanations.1: The colon after 'helloWorld' marks this as a target name in a Makefile — it's a label for a task that can be executed.
explanations.2: The 'echo' command prints text to the screen, and the tab character at the beginning is required by Makefiles to indicate this is an actual command to run (not just a comment or label).
